description: Discover the differences between living and non-living things, learn about the characteristics of life, basic needs of organisms, and explore examples from everyday life

slides.title: Welcome to Living vs Non-living Things
slides.content:
# Let's Explore the World Around Us!

Look around you right now. What do you see?

You might see a **dog**, a **tree**, a **chair**, or a **rock**.

Some of these things are **alive** and some are **not alive**.

## In This Lesson, You Will Learn:
- What makes something **living**
- What makes something **non-living**
- How to tell the difference
- What living things need to survive
- Fun examples from your daily life

> **Think About It:** Is a robot alive? Is a seed alive? By the end of this lesson, you will know the answers!

Let's begin our exciting journey!

slides.title: What Are Living Things?
slides.content:
# What Are Living Things?

**Living things** are organisms that are alive. They can do special things that non-living things cannot do.

## Examples of Living Things:
- **Animals:** Dogs, cats, birds, fish, insects
- **Plants:** Trees, flowers, grass, bushes
- **Tiny organisms:** Germs and bacteria (too small to see!)
- **Humans:** You and me!

## What Makes Something Living?

All living things share some **special abilities** called **characteristics of life**.

These are like a checklist. If something can do ALL of these things, it is **living**.

> **Fun Fact:** Scientists estimate there are about 8.7 million different species of living things on Earth!

## Can You Think of 5 Living Things Around You?

Look around your room or outside the window. Try to name 5 living things you can see right now!

slides.title: Characteristics of Living Things - Part 1
slides.content:
# Characteristics of Living Things (Part 1)

Living things have **special features** that make them different from non-living things.

## 1. Living Things GROW
- A tiny seed grows into a big tree
- A baby grows into an adult
- A puppy grows into a dog
- Growth means getting **bigger** and **more developed** over time

## 2. Living Things BREATHE
- Animals breathe in **oxygen** and breathe out **carbon dioxide**
- Plants also breathe! They take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen
- Fish breathe through their **gills** underwater
- We breathe through our **lungs**

## 3. Living Things NEED FOOD
- Animals eat plants or other animals
- Plants make their own food using **sunlight**
- Food gives living things **energy** to do everything
- Without food, living things cannot survive

> **Amazing Fact:** A blue whale eats about 4 tons of food every single day!

slides.title: Characteristics of Living Things - Part 2
slides.content:
# Characteristics of Living Things (Part 2)

Let's learn more special things that living organisms can do!

## 4. Living Things MOVE
- Animals walk, run, fly, or swim
- Plants move slowly toward sunlight
- Even tiny organisms can move around
- Movement helps living things find food and stay safe

## 5. Living Things REPRODUCE
- Reproduce means to make **babies** or **new living things**
- Animals have baby animals
- Plants make seeds that grow into new plants
- This is how life continues on Earth

## 6. Living Things RESPOND
- Living things can **feel** and **react** to things around them
- A plant grows toward light
- You pull your hand away from something hot
- A cat runs when it hears a loud noise

## 7. Living Things Eventually DIE
- All living things have a **life span**
- Some live for a few days, others for hundreds of years

> **Did You Know:** A tortoise can live for over 150 years!

slides.title: What Are Non-living Things?
slides.content:
# What Are Non-living Things?

**Non-living things** are objects that are NOT alive. They do not have the characteristics of life.

## Examples of Non-living Things:
- **Natural:** Rocks, water, air, sand, mountains
- **Man-made:** Tables, chairs, books, cars, toys
- **Materials:** Metal, plastic, glass, rubber

## What Non-living Things CANNOT Do:
- They cannot **grow** on their own
- They do not **breathe**
- They do not need **food**
- They cannot **reproduce** (make more of themselves)
- They do not **respond** to the world around them
- They do not **die** (but they can break or wear out)

## Important Note:
Some non-living things can SEEM alive:
- A **car** moves, but it needs fuel and a driver
- A **fan** moves, but it needs electricity
- A **river** flows, but it is not alive

> **Think About It:** A car moves and needs fuel like food. But is it alive? No! It cannot grow, breathe, or have baby cars!

slides.title: Differences Between Living and Non-living
slides.content:
# Living vs Non-living: The Big Comparison

Let's put living and non-living things side by side to see the differences clearly.

## Comparison Table:

| Feature | Living Things | Non-living Things |
|---------|--------------|------------------|
| Growth | Grow and develop | Do not grow |
| Breathing | Need air to breathe | Do not breathe |
| Food | Need food for energy | Do not need food |
| Movement | Can move on their own | Cannot move by themselves |
| Reproduction | Can make babies | Cannot reproduce |
| Response | React to surroundings | Do not respond |
| Death | Eventually die | Do not die (can break) |
| Cells | Made of tiny cells | Not made of cells |

## Key Rule to Remember:

If something can do **ALL** the characteristics of life, it is **living**.

If it **cannot** do even one of them on its own, it is **non-living**.

## The Easy Test:
Ask yourself: **Can it grow, breathe, eat, move, and have babies on its own?**
- YES to all = Living
- NO to any = Non-living

slides.title: Basic Needs of Living Organisms - Food
slides.content:
# What Do Living Things Need? - FOOD

All living things need certain things to stay alive. Let's learn about them one by one.

## Need 1: FOOD

Food gives living things the **energy** they need to do everything.

### How Different Living Things Get Food:

**Animals:**
- **Herbivores** eat plants (cows, rabbits, deer)
- **Carnivores** eat other animals (lions, eagles, sharks)
- **Omnivores** eat both plants and animals (bears, humans, pigs)

**Plants:**
- Plants are AMAZING - they make their own food!
- They use **sunlight**, **water**, and **air** to make food
- This process is called **photosynthesis**
- That is why plants need sunlight to survive

## What Food Does for Living Things:
- Gives **energy** to move, grow, and play
- Helps **repair** damaged parts of the body
- Helps living things **grow** bigger and stronger
- Keeps living things **healthy**

> **Think About It:** What would happen if you did not eat for a whole day? You would feel weak and tired. That shows how important food is!

slides.title: Basic Needs - Water and Air
slides.content:
# What Do Living Things Need? - WATER and AIR

## Need 2: WATER

Water is essential for all living things.

### Why Water Is Important:
- Our bodies are made up of about **70% water**
- Water helps **digest food**
- Water keeps the body **cool**
- Plants use water to make food
- Without water, living things will die in just a few days

### How Living Things Get Water:
- Animals **drink** water from rivers, lakes, and ponds
- Plants **absorb** water through their roots
- Some desert animals get water from the food they eat

## Need 3: AIR

Air contains **oxygen** that living things need to breathe.

### Why Air Is Important:
- Animals breathe in oxygen to get energy from food
- Plants use carbon dioxide from air to make food
- Without air, most living things cannot survive even a few minutes

### How Living Things Breathe:
- Humans and many animals use **lungs**
- Fish use **gills** to breathe underwater
- Insects breathe through tiny holes in their bodies
- Plants breathe through tiny pores in their **leaves**

> **Amazing Fact:** You breathe about 20,000 times every day!

slides.title: Basic Needs - Shelter and Sunlight
slides.content:
# What Do Living Things Need? - SHELTER and SUNLIGHT

## Need 4: SHELTER

Living things need a **safe place** to live, called a shelter or **habitat**.

### Animal Shelters:
- Birds build **nests** in trees
- Rabbits dig **burrows** underground
- Bears live in **caves**
- Fish live in **water** (ponds, rivers, oceans)
- Bees live in **hives**

### Plant Shelters:
- Plants grow in **soil** which is their home
- Some plants grow on other plants
- Aquatic plants live in water

### Why Shelter Matters:
- Protection from **weather** (rain, heat, cold)
- Safety from **predators** and danger
- A place to **rest** and sleep
- A place to **raise babies**

## Need 5: SUNLIGHT

- Plants MUST have sunlight to make food
- Animals need sunlight for warmth and health
- Sunlight helps our bodies make **Vitamin D**
- The sun drives the water cycle that brings rain

> **Did You Know:** Some animals, like owls and bats, prefer to be active at night. But they still depend on the sun because their food (mice, insects) depends on sunlight!

slides.title: Examples from Daily Life - Living Things
slides.content:
# Living Things in Your Daily Life

Let's explore the living things you see every single day!

## At Home:
- **Pets:** Dogs, cats, fish, hamsters, parrots
- **Plants:** Potted flowers, garden plants, herbs
- **Tiny Creatures:** Ants, flies, mosquitoes, spiders
- **Food Plants:** Fruits and vegetables in the kitchen

## At School:
- **Trees** in the playground
- **Grass** on the field
- **Birds** flying overhead
- **Insects** in the garden
- **Your friends and teachers** are living things too!

## In Nature:
- **Forest animals:** Deer, foxes, squirrels, bears
- **Ocean life:** Whales, dolphins, coral, seaweed
- **Garden creatures:** Butterflies, worms, ladybugs
- **Pond life:** Frogs, turtles, fish, water plants

## How Do We Know They Are Living?
Let's check with a dog:
- Does it grow? **YES** (puppy to adult dog)
- Does it breathe? **YES**
- Does it eat? **YES**
- Does it move? **YES**
- Can it have babies? **YES**
- Does it respond? **YES** (wags tail when happy)

> **Activity:** Pick any living thing near you and check all the characteristics of life. Does it pass the test?

slides.title: Examples from Daily Life - Non-living Things
slides.content:
# Non-living Things in Your Daily Life

Non-living things are everywhere around us too!

## At Home:
- **Furniture:** Tables, chairs, beds, shelves
- **Electronics:** TV, phone, computer, fan
- **Kitchen Items:** Plates, cups, spoons, pots
- **Toys:** Dolls, balls, building blocks, puzzles

## At School:
- **Stationery:** Pencils, erasers, rulers, crayons
- **Classroom Items:** Desks, blackboard, chalk
- **Books** and notebooks
- **The school building** itself

## In Nature:
- **Rocks** and stones
- **Water** in rivers and oceans
- **Sand** on the beach
- **Mountains** and hills
- **Wind** and clouds

## The Tricky Ones:

| Object | Seems Alive? | Actually Living? | Why? |
|--------|-------------|-------------------|------|
| Robot | Yes (moves) | No | Needs batteries, cannot grow |
| Fire | Yes (moves, grows) | No | Not made of cells, cannot reproduce |
| Cloud | Yes (moves) | No | Just water droplets in the air |
| Car | Yes (moves, uses fuel) | No | Man-made machine |

> **Remember:** Just because something moves does not mean it is alive!

slides.title: Once Living Things
slides.content:
# Once Living Things

Here is an interesting idea: Some things were ONCE alive but are no longer living!

## Examples of Once Living Things:
- **Dry leaves** that have fallen from a tree
- **A wooden table** (made from a tree that was alive)
- **Leather shoes** (made from animal skin)
- **Cotton clothes** (made from cotton plant)
- **A fossil** (remains of an ancient animal or plant)
- **Coal** (made from ancient plants millions of years ago)
- **Dead insects** you might find on a windowsill

## Three Categories:

### 1. Living Things
- Currently alive
- Examples: A growing tree, a swimming fish

### 2. Non-living Things
- Were NEVER alive
- Examples: A rock, water, a metal spoon

### 3. Once Living Things
- Were alive before but are now dead or made from dead things
- Examples: Wooden furniture, wool sweater, dried flowers

> **Brain Teaser:** Is a piece of paper living, non-living, or once living? Answer: Once living! Paper is made from trees, which were alive!

slides.title: Habitats - Where Living Things Live
slides.content:
# Habitats: Homes for Living Things

A **habitat** is the natural home or environment where a living thing lives.

## Types of Habitats:

### Land Habitats:
- **Forest:** Trees, deer, birds, insects, bears
- **Desert:** Camels, cacti, lizards, scorpions
- **Grassland:** Lions, zebras, elephants, grass
- **Arctic:** Polar bears, penguins, seals, snow owls

### Water Habitats:
- **Ocean:** Whales, sharks, coral, jellyfish
- **Freshwater (ponds/rivers):** Frogs, fish, turtles, water lilies
- **Wetlands:** Crocodiles, herons, mangrove trees

## Why Habitats Matter:
- Each habitat provides the right **food** for its living things
- It provides the right **temperature** and **weather**
- It gives **shelter** and **safety**
- Living things are **adapted** to their habitat

## What Happens When Habitats Are Destroyed?
- Animals lose their homes
- Plants cannot grow
- Living things may **die** or have to **move away**
- This is why we must **protect** nature!

> **Be a Hero:** You can help protect habitats by not littering, planting trees, and saving water!

slides.title: How Living Things Depend on Non-living Things
slides.content:
# Living Things Need Non-living Things!

Here is an important connection: **Living things depend on non-living things to survive!**

## How Plants Depend on Non-living Things:
- **Sunlight** - to make food
- **Water** - to grow and make food
- **Air** (carbon dioxide) - to make food
- **Soil** - to get nutrients and support

## How Animals Depend on Non-living Things:
- **Water** - to drink and stay hydrated
- **Air** (oxygen) - to breathe
- **Sunlight** - for warmth and health
- **Rocks and soil** - for shelter (burrows, caves)

## How Humans Depend on Non-living Things:
- **Water** - for drinking, cooking, cleaning
- **Air** - for breathing
- **Minerals** - for building tools and machines
- **Fossil fuels** - for energy (though we should use less!)

## The Big Connection:
Living and non-living things work **together** in nature:
- Plants use non-living water and sunlight to grow
- Animals eat the plants
- When animals die, they return nutrients to the soil
- The cycle continues!

> **Key Idea:** Everything in nature is connected. Living things cannot exist without non-living things!

slides.title: Fun Activities and Experiments
slides.content:
# Fun Ways to Learn About Living and Non-living Things!

## Activity 1: The Sorting Game
Collect 10 objects from your home or garden. Sort them into three groups:
- **Living**
- **Non-living**
- **Once Living**

## Activity 2: Nature Walk
Go for a walk outside and make a list:
- Write down every **living thing** you see
- Write down every **non-living thing** you see
- Which list is longer?

## Activity 3: The Plant Experiment
Plant a seed in a pot and watch it grow!
- Water it every day
- Keep it near a window for sunlight
- Write down what you see each week
- This proves that seeds are **living things**

## Activity 4: Ask the Questions
For any object, ask these 7 questions:
1. Does it grow?
2. Does it breathe?
3. Does it need food?
4. Can it move on its own?
5. Can it reproduce?
6. Does it respond to its surroundings?
7. Will it eventually die?

If the answer is **YES to all**, it is a **living thing**!

> **Challenge:** Can you find something that is tricky to classify? Discuss it with your friends or teacher!

slides.title: Common Mistakes to Avoid
slides.content:
# Common Mistakes About Living and Non-living Things

Many students get confused about certain things. Let's clear up the confusion!

## Mistake 1: "If it moves, it is alive"
- **Wrong!** A car moves but is not alive
- **Right!** Movement alone does not make something living

## Mistake 2: "Seeds are non-living"
- **Wrong!** Seeds are living things that are just **waiting** to grow
- **Right!** Seeds are alive - they just need water and warmth to start growing

## Mistake 3: "Dried flowers are living"
- **Wrong!** Once flowers are dried, they are no longer alive
- **Right!** Dried flowers are "once living" things

## Mistake 4: "Clouds are alive because they move"
- **Wrong!** Clouds are just tiny water drops carried by wind
- **Right!** Clouds are non-living things

## Mistake 5: "Fire is alive because it grows and needs air"
- **Wrong!** Fire is a chemical reaction, not a living thing
- **Right!** Fire is non-living - it is not made of cells

## The Golden Rule:
To be truly **living**, something must have **ALL** the characteristics of life, not just one or two.

> **Pro Tip:** When in doubt, ask: Is it made of **cells**? Living things are always made of tiny building blocks called cells!

slides.title: Summary and Review
slides.content:
# Summary: Living vs Non-living Things

## Key Points to Remember:

### Characteristics of Living Things:
1. They **grow** and develop
2. They **breathe** (need air)
3. They need **food** for energy
4. They can **move** on their own
5. They can **reproduce** (make babies)
6. They **respond** to their environment
7. They eventually **die**
8. They are made of **cells**

### Non-living Things:
- Do NOT have the characteristics of life
- Can be **natural** (rocks, water) or **man-made** (toys, cars)

### Once Living Things:
- Were alive at some point but are no longer living
- Examples: wood, leather, dried leaves

### Basic Needs of Living Things:
| Need | Why? |
|------|------|
| Food | Energy to live and grow |
| Water | Body processes and cooling |
| Air | Breathing and energy release |
| Shelter | Protection and safety |
| Sunlight | Warmth and food (for plants) |

### The Connection:
- Living things **depend on** non-living things
- Everything in nature is **connected**

> **Congratulations!** You now know how to tell the difference between living and non-living things. You are becoming a real scientist!
